 Search The Site Gear Up For Game Day: UNLV Rebels Gear Up For Game Day: UNLV Rebels
 Cody Tucker Cody Tucker Published: November 6, 2026 LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 27: Running back Trey Smith #7 of the Wyoming Cowboys runs against defensive back Bryce Jackson #24 of the UNLV Rebels in the second half of their game at Allegiant Stadium on November 27, 2020 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cowboys defeated the Rebels 45-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 LAS VEGAS -- The last time the Cowboys won inside Allegiant Stadium, no one was there to see it.
 7220 Sports In the first-ever trip to UNLV's new $2 billion digs -- thanks, Raiders -- quarterback Levi Williams rushed for three touchdowns and running backs Xazavian Valladay , Trey Smith and even Brett Brenton found the end zone in a 45-14 rout of the Rebels.
 The official attendance that day was zero. Why? COVID-19.
 Much has changed in the desert since that beatdown.
 Marcus Arroyo lasted two more seasons on the sideline in Sin City. He was replaced by Barry Odom . During his two-year stint, the Rebels posted 19 victories and just three losses in Mountain West play. One of those was a 34-14 win over the Cowboys in November of 2023. He eventually bolted for Purdue.
 Enter Dan Mullen .
 The former Utah assistant, who was 2-0 against Wyoming as Alex Smith's quarterback coach from 2003-04, escaped hail-covered Laramie last fall with a 31-27 outcome. Mullen is now 15-7 overall since his arrival and, like Odom, has suffered only three setbacks inside the conference.
 One of the original members of this newly-formed league back in 1999, UNLV's first two-plus decades were less than stellar. In fact, no one lost more. Those 212 shortfalls are still 23 more than a Cowboy program that is 47 games under .500.
 Under five different bosses -- John Robinson , Mike Sanford , Bobby Hauck , Tony Sanchez and Arroyo -- the Rebels were 86-197 overall. That included a 51-132 mark in league play.
 There were only a pair of postseason appearances during that stretch. The high-water mark was eight victories. Robinson's squad did that in 2000.
 UNLV won the first five conference meetings against Wyoming. The Vic Koenning era, am I right?
 There have been some other memorable matchups despite the overall records. Five of these games -- all in Las Vegas -- have needed extra time to sort out. One of those happened in 2016 when the Cowboy had a young gunslinger named Josh Allen under center.
 On a sun-splashed afternoon inside Sam Boyd Stadium, these two combined for 135 points and it took three overtime periods to decide. "I needed a drink after that one," Sanchez told 7220sports.com back in the summer of 2019.
 That sentence summed it all up.
 Josh Allen drove the Cowboys 97 yards in nine plays with just 1:06 remaining to force the first extra frame. Tanner Gentry snagged a 19-yard scoring strike with an acrobatic one-handed grab in the corner of the end zone.
 "I thought, 'they have 97 yards to go and no timeouts. We got this,'" Sanchez added. "Then they drive down the field and Gentry makes another circus catch for a darn touchdown. That was the craziest game I have ever been a part of."
 Gentry finished the day with five catches for 184 yards and three touchdowns. Allen threw for 334 yards and four touchdowns.
 That game had it all.
 Brian Hill eclipsed the 100-yard mark and scored three times. Austin Conway returned a punt 60 yards for a touchdown, too. Wyoming's defense surrendered 653 yards of total offense in the loss. The Cowboys also turned the ball over four times as the Rebels escaped with the 69-66 victory.
 Allen and Co. got the last laugh, representing the Mountain Division and hosting the conference championship game. UNLV won four games that season.
 This time around it's both teams that have title aspirations. The winner Saturday night will put itself in a prime spot to reach that goal.
 Here is all you need to know -- and the links -- for Saturday night's tilt in Sin City: 
 WHO:  Wyoming   (5-3, 4-1) at UNLV  (5-3, 3-1)
 WHEN:  Saturday, Nov. 7 at 8:30 p.m. MST
 WEATHER:  High of 76, Low 51, Sunny, Wind 5 mph (Game indoors) 
 WHERE:   Allegiant Stadium , Las Vegas, Nev.   (65,000 capacity) 
 TRAVEL:   NVroads 
 STREAMING: CBS Sports Network 
 TV: CBS Sports Network 
 RADIO:  Cowboy Sports Network 
 TICKETS:  UNLV Ticket Office 
 BOX SCORE:  ESPN 
 ROSTERS:  Wyoming  / UNLV 
 HISTORY:   Wyoming leads all-time series, 14-13 
 BETTING ODDS: UNLV -6, O/U: 48.5 
 HEAD COACHES:  Jay Sawvel   /   Dan Mullen
